mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically has led to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically results in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the GDP is increasing, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production by more than 1% in a month indicates a contraction in supply, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it signals a potential economic downturn.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO decreases and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month and retail sales (RSAFS) also increase by more than 1% in the same month, it signals a strong consumer demand, which historically has led to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increase > 5% and RSAFS increase > 1% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint correlation between HOUST and RSAFS increases and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% in the same month, signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint correlation between PAYEMS decrease, UNRATE increase, and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure coupled with tight monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month and FEDFUNDS > 2%
regime_hint: inflationary pressure with tight monetary policy
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint correlation between CPIAUCSL increases, high FEDFUNDS, and negative SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consistent increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer spending, which historically has led to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between RSAFS growth and positive SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
